'''Germán Sierra''' is a [[Spaniards|Spanish]] [[Theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]], author, and academic. He is Professor of Research at the Institute of Theoretical Physics Autonomous [[Complutense University of Madrid|University of Madrid]]-[[Spanish National Research Council]].<ref name=FGS>{{Cite web|url=https://fulbrightscholars.org/grantee/francisco-german-sierra-rodero|title=Francisco German Sierra Rodero &#124; Fulbright Scholar Program|website=fulbrightscholars.org}}</ref>

Sierra's research interests span the field of [[physics]] and [[mathematical physics]], focusing particularly on [[condensed matter physics]], [[conformal field theory]], exactly solved models, [[quantum information]] and [[Computational complexity theory|computation]] and [[number theory]]. He has authored two books entitled, ''Quantum Groups in Two-dimensional Physics'' and ''Quantum electron liquids and high-Tc Superconductivity''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.worldcat.org/title/33359250|title=Quantum electron liquids and high-Tc superconductivity &#124; WorldCat.org|website=www.worldcat.org}}</ref> and also has published over 200 articles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=fTRtZE8AAAAJ&hl=en|title=German Sierra Rodero|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

Sierra serves as an Editor of the ''Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment'',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/journal/1742-5468/page/editorial_board
|title=Editorial Board - Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment
|website=IOPscience
|access-date=September 14, 2026
}}</ref> ''Journal of High Energy Physics''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.springer.com/journal/13130/editors| title= Editor}}</ref> and ''Nuclear Physics B''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/nuclear-physics-b/about/editorial-board|title=Editorial board – Nuclear Physics B &#124; ScienceDirect.com by Elsevier|website=www.sciencedirect.com}}</ref>

==Education==
Sierra earned his Baccalaureate degree in physics from the University of Complutense de Madrid in 1978, followed by a Ph.D. in physics from the same university in 1981. He then completed his Postdoc from the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|l'École Normale Supérieure]] in [[Paris]] in 1983.<ref name=FGS/>

==Career==
Following his Postdoc, Sierra began his academic career as a Titular Professor at the University of Complutense de Madrid in 1984, a position he held for 
three years. In 1987 he was appointed as a research fellow at the [[CERN|European Council for Nuclear Research (CERN)]] in [[Geneva]] and as a Scientific Researcher at Spanish National Research Council in 1989. Since 2005, he has been serving as a Full Professor of Physics at the Spanish National Research Council in Spain.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ift.uam-csic.es/es/one-member/172|title=Instituto de Física Teórica &#124; Centro de excelencia Severo Ochoa|website=www.ift.uam-csic.es}}</ref> He has held visiting appointments at [[Erwin Schrödinger]] Institute,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.esi.ac.at/static/assets/extras/reports/ESI_Report_2018.8c1a71c8c3b3.pdf|title=Annual Report 2018}}</ref> [[Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kitp.ucsb.edu/activities/lowdim97/photos|title=Kavli Institute for Theoretical Physics - Visitors Photos}}</ref> Max Planck Institute for Quantum Optics,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mpq.mpg.de/6886095/germ-n-sierra|title= Prof. German Sierra}}</ref> University of Sao Paulo,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www2.ifsc.usp.br/portal-ifsc/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Relatorio_FCM_2017.pdf|title=Relatório de Atividades 2017}}</ref> Princeton University,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fulbrightscholars.org/grantee/francisco-german-sierra-rodero|title=Francisco German Sierra Rodero}}</ref> [[Isaac Newton Institute]] for Mathematical Sciences,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newton.ac.uk/event/qim/|title=Mathematical aspects of quantum integrable models in and out of equilibrium|date=25 February 2021 }}</ref> Stony Brook University,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scgp.stonybrook.edu/archives/35461|title=Number Theory And Physics: October 24 – November 18 2022}}</ref> and [[University of Innsbruck]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uibk.ac.at/th-physik/qig_bk/news-activities/news-8.html.en|title=Welcome to German Sierra|date=30 June 2022 }}</ref>

From 2014 to 2017, he was a Member of the International Union of Pure and Applied Physics (IUPAP), Panel C18 on Mathematical Physics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://archive2.iupap.org/c18-members-2014-2017/|title=C18: MEMBERS (2014-2017)}}</ref>

==Research==

===Supergravity===
During his early research career, Sierra worked in the area of supergravity to construct and classify the N = 2 Maxwell-Einstein Supergravity theories (MESGT).<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Gauging the d = 5 Maxwell/Einstein supergravity theories: More on Jordan algebras|first1=M.|last1=Günaydin|first2=G.|last2=Sierra|first3=P. K.|last3=Townsend|date=January 1, 1985|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=253|pages=573–608|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(85)90547-4| bibcode=1985NuPhB.253..573G }}</ref> His work involved an investigation of the algebraic and geometric structures underlying these theories, as well as their compact and non-compact gaugings.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://inis.iaea.org/search/search.aspx?orig_q=RN:17060477|title=N = 2 Maxwell-Einstein Supergravity theories: their compact and non-compact gaugings and Jordan algebras|first1=Guenaydin|last1=M.|first2=Sierra|last2=G.|first3=Townsend|last3=P.K.|date=August 7, 1985}}</ref> In collaboration with M. Gunaydin and P.K. Townsend, he derived the magic square of Freudenthal, Rozenfeld, and Tits by utilizing the geometric principles found in a specific group of N=2 Maxwell-Einstein supergravity theories.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Exceptional supergravity theories and the magic square|first1=M.|last1=Günaydin|first2=G.|last2=Sierra|first3=P. K.|last3=Townsend|date=December 8, 1983|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=133|issue=1|pages=72–76|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(83)90108-9|bibcode=1983PhLB..133...72G }}</ref>

===Quantum groups===
In 1990, Sierra's research diverted toward the construction, interpretation, and application of quantum groups<ref>{{Cite book|chapter-url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/9789814534314|chapter=Generalized Symmetries in Physics|first1=H.-D.|last1=Doebner|first2=V. K.|last2=Dobrev|first3=A. G.|last3=Ushveridze|date=July 7, 1994|publisher=World Scientific|pages=1–444|via=worldscientific.com (Atypon)|doi=10.1142/9789814534314|isbn=978-981-02-1771-6 }}</ref> in the context of conformal field theories,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://inis.iaea.org/search/search.aspx?orig_q=RN:23050325|title=Duality and quantum groups|first=Sierra|last=G.|date=August 7, 1989|pages=417–446 }}</ref> two-dimensional physics,<ref>{{Cite book|first=German|last=Sierra|url=https://www.academia.edu/79250741|title=Quantum Groups in Two-Dimensional Physics|date=1996 |isbn=978-0-511-62882-5 |via=[[Academia.edu]]}}</ref> and renormalization groups.<ref name="auto">{{Cite book|chapter-url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/9789814527293|chapter=The Exact Renormalization Group|first1=A.|last1=Krasnitz|first2=Y. A.|last2=Kubyshin|first3=R.|last3=Potting|first4=P.|last4=Sá|date=August 7, 1999|publisher=WORLD SCIENTIFIC|pages=1–238|via=worldscientific.com (Atypon)|doi=10.1142/9789814527293|isbn=978-981-02-3939-8 }}</ref> He demonstrated that the representation theory of the q-deformation of SU(2) offers solutions to the polynomial equations formulated by Moore and Seiberg for rational conformal field theories, as long as q is a [[root of unity]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Quantum group interpretation of some conformal field theories|first1=L.|last1=Alvarez-Gaumé|first2=C.|last2=Gomez|first3=G.|last3=Sierra|date=March 30, 1989|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=220|issue=1|pages=142–152|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(89)90027-0|bibcode=1989PhLB..220..142A }}</ref> Together with Cesar Gomez, he defined the representation spaces of the quantum group in terms of screened vertex operators and interpreted the number of screening operators as the genuine quantum group number.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Quantum group meaning of the Coulomb gas|first1=César|last1=Gómez|first2=Germán|last2=Sierra|date=April 19, 1990|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=240|issue=1|pages=149–157|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(90)90424-5|bibcode=1990PhLB..240..149G }}</ref> He introduced a spin chain Hamiltonian that possesses integrability and invariance under 14 (sI(2)) transformations within nilpotent irreducible representations when r3 = 1.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=On integrable quantum group invariant antiferromagnets|first1=R.|last1=Cuerno|first2=G.|last2=Sierra|first3=C.|last3=Gómez|date=June 1, 1993|journal=Journal of Geometry and Physics|volume=11|issue=1|pages=453–462|doi=10.1016/0393-0440(93)90071-L|arxiv=hep-th/9205109 |bibcode=1993JGP....11..453C |hdl=10016/7155 |s2cid=119448576 }}</ref> Additionally, he proved that the elliptic R-matrix of the eight vertex free fermion model is the intertwiner R-matrix of a quantum deformed Clifford-Hopf algebra that the elliptic R-matrix of the eight-vertex free fermion model corresponds to the intertwiner R-matrix of a quantum deformed Clifford-Hopf algebra.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=The hidden quantum group of the eight-vertex free fermion model: q-Clifford algebras|first1=R.|last1=Cuerno|first2=C.|last2=Gómez|first3=E.|last3=López|first4=G.|last4=Sierra|date=June 10, 1993|journal=Physics Letters B|volume=307|issue=1|pages=56–60|doi=10.1016/0370-2693(93)90192-K|arxiv=hep-th/9302089 |bibcode=1993PhLB..307...56C |hdl=10016/7151 |s2cid=119488308 }}</ref> In his work, he also presented a new mathematical structure entitled, graph quantum group which merges the tower of algebras associated with a graph G with the structure of a Hopf algebra {\cal A}.<ref>{{Cite arXiv|title=Graph Quantum Groups|first1=C.|last1=Gomez|first2=G.|last2=Sierra|date=December 22, 1993|eprint=hep-th/9312177 }}</ref> Furthermore, he explored spin-anisotropy commensurable chains, a class of 2D integrable models, and described their mathematics using quantum groups with the deformation parameter as an Nth root of unity.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Spin-anisotropy commensurable chains. Quantum group symmetries and N = 2 SUSY|first1=Alexander|last1=Bérkovich|first2=César|last2=Gómez|first3=Germán|last3=Sierra|date=March 14, 1994|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=415|issue=3|pages=681–733|doi=10.1016/0550-3213(94)90307-7| arxiv=hep-th/9302001 | bibcode=1994NuPhB.415..681B | s2cid=119328363 }}</ref> Moreover, alongside Miguel A. Martín-Delgado, he employed real space [[renormalization group]] (RG) methods<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.1146|title=Real Space Renormalization Group Methods and Quantum Groups|first1=Miguel A.|last1=Martín-Delgado|first2=Germán|last2=Sierra|date=February 12, 1996|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=76|issue=7|pages=1146–1149|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.1146|pmid=10061645 |arxiv=cond-mat/9507115 |bibcode=1996PhRvL..76.1146M |hdl=10261/102722 |s2cid=7812291 }}</ref> to examine the interplay between two different variants of quantum groups, exploring their relationship.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/9789812830425_0007|title=From Field Theory to Quantum Groups|first1=Miguel A.|last1=Mart?n-Delgado|first2=Germ?n|last2=Sierra|chapter=The renormalization group method and quantum groups: The postman always rings twice |date=June 7, 1996|publisher=WORLD SCIENTIFIC|pages=113–139|via=worldscientific.com (Atypon)|doi=10.1142/9789812830425_0007|arxiv=hep-th/9511190 |isbn=978-981-02-2544-5 |s2cid=15210167 }}</ref>

===Spin chains and ladders===
In 1996, Sierra started working in condensed matter physics, more concretely on spin chains, spin ladders and high-Tc superconductors. He generalized Haldane's conjecture from spin chains to spin ladders using the O(3) non-linear sigma model.<ref name=ggg/> He also investigated phase transitions in staggered spin ladders<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3443|title=Phase Transitions in Staggered Spin Ladders|first1=M. A.|last1=Martín-Delgado|first2=R.|last2=Shankar|first3=G.|last3=Sierra|date=October 14, 1996|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=77|issue=16|pages=3443–3446|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.3443|pmid=10062221 |bibcode=1996PhRvL..77.3443M |hdl=10261/102696 |hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0375960198008494|title=Phase diagram of the 2-leg Heisenberg ladder with alternating dimerization|first1=M. A.|last1=Martín-Delgado|first2=J.|last2=Dukelsky|first3=G.|last3=Sierra|date=December 28, 1998|journal=Physics Letters A|volume=250|issue=4|pages=430–434|via=ScienceDirect|doi=10.1016/S0375-9601(98)00849-4|arxiv=cond-mat/9810379 |bibcode=1998PhLA..250..430M |hdl=10261/100639 |s2cid=39479040 }}</ref> and three-legged antiferromagnetic ladders.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.55.R3340|title=Low-energy properties of antiferromagnetic spin-1/2 Heisenberg ladders with an odd number of legs|first1=Beat|last1=Frischmuth|first2=Stephan|last2=Haas|first3=German|last3=Sierra|first4=T. M.|last4=Rice|date=February 1, 1997|journal=Physical Review B|volume=55|issue=6|pages=R3340–R3343|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.55.R3340|arxiv=cond-mat/9606183 |bibcode=1997PhRvB..55.3340F |s2cid=119074714 }}</ref> In addition, he applied the variational matrix product ansatz to determine the ground state of several ladder systems.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.56.8774|title=Short-range resonating-valence-bond state of even-spin ladders: A recurrent variational approach|first1=Germán|last1=Sierra|first2=Miguel A.|last2=Martín-Delgado|date=October 1, 1997|journal=Physical Review B|volume=56|issue=14|pages=8774–8785|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.56.8774|arxiv=cond-mat/9704212 |bibcode=1997PhRvB..56.8774S |s2cid=15281550 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.64.075117|title=Stripe ans\"atze from exactly solved models|first1=M. A.|last1=Martín-Delgado|first2=M.|last2=Roncaglia|first3=G.|last3=Sierra|date=July 31, 2001|journal=Physical Review B|volume=64|issue=7|article-number=075117|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.64.075117|arxiv=cond-mat/0101458 |bibcode=2001PhRvB..64g5117M |s2cid=14541090 }}</ref> In a joint study with J. Dukelsky, M.A. Martín-Delgado and T. Nishino, he showed that the latter method is equivalent to the DMRG method introduced by S. R. White in 1992.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1209/epl/i1998-00381-x/meta|doi=10.1209/epl/i1998-00381-x |title=Equivalence of the variational matrix product method and the density matrix renormalization group applied to spin chains |date=1998 |last1=Dukelsky |first1=J. |last2=Martín-Delgado |first2=M. A. |last3=Nishino |first3=T. |last4=Sierra |first4=G. |journal=Europhysics Letters |volume=43 |issue=4 |pages=457–462 |arxiv=cond-mat/9710310 |bibcode=1998EL.....43..457D |hdl=10261/100542 |s2cid=250914148 }}</ref> Working together with Martín-Delgado in 1998, he proposed an extension of the variational matrix product ansatzs to two dimensions.<ref name="auto"/> In 2004, F. Verstraete and J.I. Cirac rediscovered the latter ansatz using quantum information techniques, designating it as PEPS.<ref>{{Cite arXiv|title=Renormalization algorithms for Quantum-Many Body Systems in two and higher dimensions|first1=F.|last1=Verstraete|first2=J. I.|last2=Cirac|date=July 2, 2004|eprint=cond-mat/0407066 }}</ref>

===Richardson-Gaudin models===
In 1999, Sierra in collaboration with J. Dukelsky applied the DMRG method to the pairing model that describes ultrasmall superconducting grains,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.61.12302|title=Crossover from bulk to few-electron limit in ultrasmall metallic grains|first1=J.|last1=Dukelsky|first2=G.|last2=Sierra|date=May 1, 2000|journal=Physical Review B|volume=61|issue=18|pages=12302–12314|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.61.12302|arxiv=cond-mat/9906166 |bibcode=2000PhRvB..6112302D |hdl=10261/96600 |s2cid=10931592 }}</ref> confirming the exact solution of the pairing model obtained by Richardson and Sherman in 1963–64.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/bitstream/handle/2027.42/32238/0000300.pdf;sequence=1|title=A Restricted Class of Exact Eigenstates of the Pairing-Force Hamiltonian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=Exact eigenstates of the pairing-force Hamiltonian|first1=R. W.|last1=Richardson|first2=N.|last2=Sherman|date=March 1, 1964|journal=Nuclear Physics|volume=52|pages=221–238|doi=10.1016/0029-5582(64)90687-X|bibcode=1964NucPh..52..221R |hdl=2027.42/32140 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> Shortly after its application, a close relationship was revealed between Richardson's solution and another set of exactly solvable models called the Gaudin magnets,<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://jphys.journaldephysique.org/articles/jphys/abs/1976/10/jphys_1976__37_10_1087_0/jphys_1976__37_10_1087_0.html|title=Diagonalisation of a class of spin hamiltoniansDiagonalisation d'une classe d'hamiltoniens de spin – Journal de Physique |journal=Journal de Physique |date=October 1976 |volume=37 |issue=10 |pages=1087–1098 |doi=10.1051/jphys:0197600370100108700 |last1=Gaudin |first1=M. }}</ref> collectively known as Richardson-Gaudin models.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.76.643|title=Colloquium: Exactly solvable Richardson-Gaudin models for many-body quantum systems|first1=J.|last1=Dukelsky|first2=S.|last2=Pittel|first3=G.|last3=Sierra|date=August 6, 2004|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|volume=76|issue=3|pages=643–662|via=APS|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.76.643|arxiv=nucl-th/0405011 |bibcode=2004RvMP...76..643D |s2cid=611020 }}</ref> Several subsequent applications involved studying the effect of level statistics in nanograins,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.61.R11890|title=Exact study of the effect of level statistics in ultrasmall superconducting grains|first1=G.|last1=Sierra|first2=J.|last2=Dukelsky|first3=G. G.|last3=Dussel|first4=Jan|last4=von Delft|first5=Fabian|last5=Braun|date=May 1, 2000|journal=Physical Review B|volume=61|issue=18|pages=R11890–R11893|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.61.R11890|arxiv=cond-mat/9909015 |bibcode=2000PhRvB..6111890S |hdl=10261/96855 |s2cid=6473797 }}</ref> the connection with conformal field theory<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0550321300000365|title=Conformal field theory and the exact solution of the BCS Hamiltonian|first=Germán|last=Sierra|date=April 24, 2000|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=572|issue=3|pages=517–534|via=ScienceDirect|doi=10.1016/S0550-3213(00)00036-5|arxiv=hep-th/9911078 |bibcode=2000NuPhB.572..517S |hdl=10261/96971 |s2cid=119495901 }}</ref> and Chern-Simons theory,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0550321301006149|title=Chern–Simons theory and BCS superconductivity|first1=Manuel|last1=Asorey|first2=Fernando|last2=Falceto|first3=Germán|last3=Sierra|date=February 11, 2002|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=622|issue=3|pages=593–614|via=ScienceDirect|doi=10.1016/S0550-3213(01)00614-9|arxiv=hep-th/0110266 |bibcode=2002NuPhB.622..593A |s2cid=17782590 }}</ref> as well as exploring the implications with mean-field solutions<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0550321302003176|title=Large-N limit of the exactly solvable BCS model: analytics versus numerics|first1=J. M.|last1=Román|first2=G.|last2=Sierra|first3=J.|last3=Dukelsky|date=July 15, 2002|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=634|issue=3|pages=483–510|via=ScienceDirect|doi=10.1016/S0550-3213(02)00317-6|arxiv=cond-mat/0202070 |bibcode=2002NuPhB.634..483R |s2cid=118913100 }}</ref> and p-wave symmetry.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.79.180501|title=Exactly solvable pairing model for superconductors with ${p}_{x}+i{p}_{y}$-wave symmetry|first1=Miguel|last1=Ibañez|first2=Jon|last2=Links|first3=Germán|last3=Sierra|first4=Shao-You|last4=Zhao|date=May 1, 2009|journal=Physical Review B|volume=79|issue=18|article-number=180501|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.79.180501|arxiv=0810.0340 |hdl=10261/20555 |s2cid=119268490 |hdl-access=free}}</ref>

===Russian doll renormalization group===
In 2003–04, Sierra, in conjunction with A. LeClair and J.M. Román, introduced multiple models exhibiting a Russian doll renormalization group flow, featuring a cyclic nature instead of converging to a fixed point. Among them was a BCS model with pairing scattering phases that break time-reversal symmetry,<ref name=hjk/> which was later demonstrated to be solvable using the algebraic [[Bethe ansatz]].<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0550321304007278|title=Integrability of the Russian doll BCS model|first1=Clare|last1=Dunning|first2=Jon|last2=Links|date=December 13, 2004|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=702|issue=3|pages=481–494|via=ScienceDirect|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2004.09.021|arxiv=cond-mat/0406234 |bibcode=2004NuPhB.702..481D |s2cid=16641548 }}</ref> Moreover, they put forward two scattering S-matrices exhibiting a cyclic renormalization group (RG) structure, which is related to both the cycle regime of the Kosterlitz-Thouless flow and an analytic extension of the massive sine-Gordon S matrix.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0550321303007818|title=Russian doll renormalization group and Kosterlitz–Thouless flows|first1=André|last1=LeClair|first2=José Marı́a|last2=Román|first3=Germán|last3=Sierra|date=December 29, 2003|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=675|issue=3|pages=584–606|via=ScienceDirect|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2003.09.032|arxiv=hep-th/0301042 |bibcode=2003NuPhB.675..584L }}</ref>

===Physical models of the Riemann zeros===
In 2005, Sierra presented a Russian doll model of superconductivity whose spectrum contains the average Riemann zeros as missing spectral lines,<ref name=zzz/> and this model is connected to the xp Hamiltonian of Berry, Keating, and Connes. In addition to proposing several variations of the xp model,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0550321307002246|title=H=xp with interaction and the Riemann zeros|first=Germán|last=Sierra|date=August 6, 2007|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=776|issue=3|pages=327–364|via=ScienceDirect|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2007.03.049| arxiv=math-ph/0702034 | bibcode=2007NuPhB.776..327S | s2cid=118176000 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.101.110201|title=Landau Levels and Riemann Zeros|first1=Germán|last1=Sierra|first2=Paul K.|last2=Townsend|date=September 12, 2008|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=101|issue=11|article-number=110201|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.101.110201|pmid=18851266 |arxiv=0805.4079 |bibcode=2008PhRvL.101k0201S |hdl=10261/5531 |s2cid=2871070 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1751-8113/47/32/325204/meta|doi=10.1088/1751-8113/47/32/325204 |title=The Riemann zeros as energy levels of a Dirac fermion in a potential built from the prime numbers in Rindler spacetime |date=2014 |last1=Sierra |first1=Germán |journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical |volume=47 |issue=32 |article-number=325204 |arxiv=1404.4252 |bibcode=2014JPhA...47F5204S |s2cid=119709107 }}</ref> he collaborated with C. E. Creffield to propose a different physical realization of the Riemann zeros using periodically driven cold atoms;<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.91.063608|title=Finding zeros of the Riemann zeta function by periodic driving of cold atoms|first1=C. E.|last1=Creffield|first2=G.|last2=Sierra|date=June 8, 2015|journal=Physical Review A|volume=91|issue=6|article-number=063608|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.91.063608|arxiv=1411.0459 |bibcode=2015PhRvA..91f3608C |hdl=10486/676030 |s2cid=53331963 }}</ref> this idea was eventually experimentally achieved in 2021 using trapped ions.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Riemann zeros from a periodically-driven trapped ion|first1=Ran|last1=He|first2=Ming-Zhong|last2=Ai|first3=Jin-Ming|last3=Cui|first4=Yun-Feng|last4=Huang|first5=Yong-Jian|last5=Han|first6=Chuan-Feng|last6=Li|first7=Guang-Can|last7=Guo|first8=G.|last8=Sierra|first9=C. E.|last9=Creffield|date=July 14, 2021|journal=npj Quantum Information|volume=7|issue=1|page=109|doi=10.1038/s41534-021-00446-7|doi-access=free|arxiv=2102.06936|s2cid=256707919 }}</ref>

===Entanglement in quantum hall states===
In 2009, Sierra and I. D. Rodríguez evaluated the entanglement entropy for integer quantum Hall states, involving the computation of the entanglement spectrum, proposed by Li and Haldane<ref name=ttt/> to identify topological order in non-abelian quantum Hall states.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.80.153303|title=Entanglement entropy of integer quantum Hall states|first1=Iván D.|last1=Rodríguez|first2=Germán|last2=Sierra|date=October 7, 2009|journal=Physical Review B|volume=80|issue=15|article-number=153303|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.80.153303|arxiv=0811.2188 |bibcode=2009PhRvB..80o3303R |s2cid=118686155 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1742-5468/2010/12/P12033/meta|doi=10.1088/1742-5468/2010/12/p12033 |title=Entanglement entropy of integer quantum Hall states in polygonal domains |date=2010 |last1=Rodríguez |first1=Iván D. |last2=Sierra |first2=Germán |journal=Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment |volume=2010 |issue=12 |article-number=P12033 |arxiv=1007.5356 |bibcode=2010JSMTE..12..033R |s2cid=118477323 }}</ref>

===Entanglement in conformal field theory===
Sierra computed with F. C. Alcaraz and M. Ibáñez the entanglement properties of the low-lying excitations in conformal field theory in 2011 and found several applications to condensed matter systems, holography,<ref name=oll/><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1742-5468/2012/01/P01016/meta|doi=10.1088/1742-5468/2012/01/p01016 |title=Entanglement of excited states in critical spin chains |date=2012 |last1=Ibáñez Berganza |first1=Miguel |last2=Alcaraz |first2=Francisco Castilho |last3=Sierra |first3=Germán |journal=Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment |volume=2012 |issue=1 |article-number=P01016 |arxiv=1109.5673 |bibcode=2012JSMTE..01..016I |s2cid=119214108 }}</ref> and systems with boundaries.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.88.075112|title=Entanglement entropies in conformal systems with boundaries|first1=L.|last1=Taddia|first2=J. C.|last2=Xavier|first3=F. C.|last3=Alcaraz|first4=G.|last4=Sierra|date=August 5, 2013|journal=Physical Review B|volume=88|issue=7|article-number=075112|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.88.075112|arxiv=1302.6222 |bibcode=2013PhRvB..88g5112T |s2cid=53462122 }}</ref> Furthermore, he independently discovered with J. C. Xavier and F. C Alcaraz the property of "entanglement equipartition" in conformal systems with U(1) symmetry, where the entanglement entropy is equally distributed in different charge sectors<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.98.041106|title=Equipartition of the entanglement entropy|first1=J. C.|last1=Xavier|first2=F. C.|last2=Alcaraz|first3=G.|last3=Sierra|date=July 17, 2018|journal=Physical Review B|volume=98|issue=4|article-number=041106|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.98.041106|arxiv=1804.06357 |bibcode=2018PhRvB..98d1106X |s2cid=53490532 }}</ref> and this finding holds for more general systems up to corrections, separate from the works.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1742-5468/2014/11/P11013/meta|doi=10.1088/1742-5468/2014/11/p11013 |title=Spin-resolved entanglement spectroscopy of critical spin chains and Luttinger liquids |date=2014 |last1=Laflorencie |first1=Nicolas |last2=Rachel |first2=Stephan |journal=Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment |volume=2014 |issue=11 |article-number=P11013 |arxiv=1407.3779 |bibcode=2014JSMTE..11..013L |s2cid=119237142 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.200602|title=Symmetry-Resolved Entanglement in Many-Body Systems|first1=Moshe|last1=Goldstein|first2=Eran|last2=Sela|date=May 16, 2018|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=120|issue=20|article-number=200602|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.120.200602|pmid=29864300 |arxiv=1711.09418 |bibcode=2018PhRvL.120t0602G |s2cid=46975599 }}</ref>

===Entanglement in inhomogeneous spin chains===
In 2014, Sierra, along with J. Rodríguez-Laguna and G. Ramírez, introduced an inhomogeneous spin chain model called rainbow chain that exhibits a maximal violation of the area law of entanglement entropy, in stark contrast to the behavior observed in homogeneous chains.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1742-5468/2015/06/P06002/meta|doi=10.1088/1742-5468/2015/06/p06002 |title=Entanglement over the rainbow |date=2015 |last1=Ramírez |first1=Giovanni |last2=Rodríguez-Laguna |first2=Javier |last3=Sierra |first3=Germán |journal=Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment |volume=2015 |issue=6 |article-number=P06002 |arxiv=1503.02695 |bibcode=2015JSMTE..06..002R |s2cid=118523429 }}</ref> The rainbow chain model, earlier proposed by J. I. Latorre in a separate joint work,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1367-2630/12/11/113049/meta|doi=10.1088/1367-2630/12/11/113049 |title=Volume-law scaling for the entanglement entropy in spin-1/2 chains |date=2010 |last1=Vitagliano |first1=G. |last2=Riera |first2=A. |last3=Latorre |first3=J. I. |journal=New Journal of Physics |volume=12 |issue=11 |article-number=113049 |arxiv=1003.1292 |bibcode=2010NJPh...12k3049V |s2cid=119119917 }}</ref> was examined using conformal field theory techniques<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1751-8121/aa6268/meta|doi=10.1088/1751-8121/aa6268 |title=More on the rainbow chain: Entanglement, space-time geometry and thermal states |date=2017 |last1=Rodríguez-Laguna |first1=Javier |last2=Dubail |first2=Jérôme |last3=Ramírez |first3=Giovanni |last4=Calabrese |first4=Pasquale |last5=Sierra |first5=Germán |journal=Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical |volume=50 |issue=16 |page=164001 |arxiv=1611.08559 |bibcode=2017JPhA...50p4001R |s2cid=119225985 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1742-5468/aab67d/meta|doi=10.1088/1742-5468/aab67d |title=Entanglement hamiltonian and entanglement contour in inhomogeneous 1D critical systems |date=2018 |last1=Tonni |first1=Erik |last2=Rodríguez-Laguna |first2=Javier |last3=Sierra |first3=Germán |journal=Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment |volume=2018 |issue=4 |page=043105 |arxiv=1712.03557 |bibcode=2018JSMTE..04.3105T |s2cid=119448770 }}</ref> and was found to support symmetry-protected phases.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1742-5468/ab3192/meta|doi=10.1088/1742-5468/ab3192 |title=Symmetry protected phases in inhomogeneous spin chains |date=2019 |last1=De Buruaga |first1=Nadir Samos Sáenz |last2=Santalla |first2=Silvia N. |last3=Rodríguez-Laguna |first3=Javier |last4=Sierra |first4=Germán |journal=Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment |volume=2019 |issue=9 |page=093102 |arxiv=1812.04869 |bibcode=2019JSMTE..09.3102S |s2cid=119406881 }}</ref>

===Infinite matrix product states and conformal field theory===
In 2010, Sierra proposed a variational ansatz for the ground state of the XXZ spin chain using the chiral vertex operators of a CFT<ref name=yyy/> to describe the critical region of this model, resulting in a matrix product state with an infinite bond dimension to capture logarithmic entanglement entropy. The ansatz also replicated the Haldane-Shastry wave function for the XXX spin chain, notably matching a conformal block of the WZW model SU(2) at level k=1, and was later extended to any level k jointly with A. E. B. Nielsen and  J. Ignacio Cirac.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1742-5468/2011/11/P11014/meta|doi=10.1088/1742-5468/2011/11/p11014 |title=Quantum spin Hamiltonians for the ''SU'' (2)<sub> ''k'' </sub>WZW model |date=2011 |last1=Nielsen |first1=Anne E B. |last2=Ignacio Cirac |first2=J. |last3=Sierra |first3=Germán |journal=Journal of Statistical Mechanics: Theory and Experiment |volume=2011 |issue=11 |article-number=P11014 |arxiv=1109.5470 |bibcode=2011JSMTE..11..014N |s2cid=119223177 }}</ref> In two spatial dimensions,  the CFT wave function demonstrated a bosonic Laughlin spin liquid state on a lattice,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.108.257206|title=Laughlin Spin-Liquid States on Lattices Obtained from Conformal Field Theory|first1=Anne E. B.|last1=Nielsen|first2=J. Ignacio|last2=Cirac|first3=Germán|last3=Sierra|date=June 20, 2012|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=108|issue=25|article-number=257206|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.108.257206|pmid=23004652 |arxiv=1201.3096 |bibcode=2012PhRvL.108y7206N |s2cid=11713272 }}</ref> that was experimentally realized using optical lattices.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.nature.com/articles/ncomms3864|title=Local models of fractional quantum Hall states in lattices and physical implementation|first1=Anne E. B.|last1=Nielsen|first2=Germán|last2=Sierra|first3=J. Ignacio|last3=Cirac|date=November 28, 2013|journal=Nature Communications|volume=4|issue=1|page=2864|via=www.nature.com|doi=10.1038/ncomms3864|doi-access=free|pmid=24284969 |s2cid=118677640 |arxiv=1304.0717}}</ref> This method was extended to other bosonic and fermionic Laughlin states,<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1367-2630/16/3/033025/meta|doi=10.1088/1367-2630/16/3/033025 |title=Lattice Laughlin states of bosons and fermions at filling fractions 1/ ''q'' |date=2014 |last1=Tu |first1=Hong-Hao |last2=Nielsen |first2=Anne E B. |last3=Cirac |first3=J Ignacio |last4=Sierra |first4=Germán |journal=New Journal of Physics |volume=16 |issue=3 |article-number=033025 |arxiv=1311.3958 |bibcode=2014NJPh...16c3025T |s2cid=119202413 }}</ref>  WZW model SU(N)_1, etc.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0550321314002107|title=Quantum spin models for the SU(n)1 Wess–Zumino–Witten model|first1=Hong-Hao|last1=Tu|first2=Anne E. B.|last2=Nielsen|first3=Germán|last3=Sierra|date=September 1, 2014|journal=Nuclear Physics B|volume=886|pages=328–363|via=ScienceDirect|doi=10.1016/j.nuclphysb.2014.06.027|arxiv=1405.2950 |bibcode=2014NuPhB.886..328T |s2cid=119125729 }}</ref> The CFT wave functions described earlier were derived as tensor network states where the individual tensors are functionals of fields<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.103.155130|title=Field tensor network states|first1=Anne E. B.|last1=Nielsen|first2=Benedikt|last2=Herwerth|first3=J. Ignacio|last3=Cirac|first4=Germán|last4=Sierra|date=April 16, 2021|journal=Physical Review B|volume=103|issue=15|article-number=155130|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.103.155130|arxiv=2001.07723 |bibcode=2021PhRvB.103o5130N |s2cid=210861136 }}</ref> which allowed the analysis of the symmetries of the field tensor network states.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevB.107.155102|title=Symmetries and field tensor network states|first1=Albert|last1=Gasull|first2=Antoine|last2=Tilloy|first3=J. Ignacio|last3=Cirac|first4=Germán|last4=Sierra|date=April 3, 2023|journal=Physical Review B|volume=107|issue=15|article-number=155102|via=APS|doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.107.155102|arxiv=2209.11253 |bibcode=2023PhRvB.107o5102G |s2cid=252519432 }}</ref>

===The prime state===
Along with J. I. Latorre, Sierra proposed a quantum circuit that creates a pure state corresponding to the quantum superposition of all prime numbers less than 2^n, where n is the number of qubits of the register.<ref name=sss/> They showed the construction of the Prime state using the Gover algorithm that combined with the quantum counting algorithm allows for a verification of the Riemann hypothesis for numbers far beyond the reach of any classical computer. Moreover, the Prime state turned out to be highly entangled with an entanglement spectrum intimately related to the Hardy-Littlewood constants for the pairwise distribution of primes.<ref>{{Cite arXiv|title=There is entanglement in the primes|first1=José Ignacio|last1=Latorre|first2=Germán|last2=Sierra|date=April 7, 2014|class=quant-ph |eprint=1403.4765}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://quantum-journal.org/papers/q-2020-12-11-371/|title=The Prime state and its quantum relatives|first1=D.|last1=García-Martín|first2=E.|last2=Ribas|first3=S.|last3=Carrazza|first4=J. I.|last4=Latorre|first5=G.|last5=Sierra|date=December 11, 2020|journal=Quantum|volume=4|article-number=371|via=quantum-journal.org|doi=10.22331/q-2020-12-11-371|arxiv=2005.02422 |bibcode=2020Quant...4..371G |s2cid=218516768 }}</ref>

===Quantum computation===
Through collaborative research efforts, Sierra implemented multiple quantum algorithms on the newly launched IBM quantum computers and introduced a quantum circuit capable of generating the Bethe eigenstates for the XXZ Hamiltonian.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://quantum-journal.org/papers/q-2022-09-08-796/|title=Algebraic Bethe Circuits|first1=Alejandro|last1=Sopena|first2=Max Hunter|last2=Gordon|first3=Diego|last3=García-Martín|first4=Germán|last4=Sierra|first5=Esperanza|last5=López|date=September 8, 2022|journal=Quantum|volume=6|article-number=796|via=quantum-journal.org|doi=10.22331/q-2022-09-08-796|arxiv=2202.04673 |bibcode=2022Quant...6..796S |s2cid=246706299 }}</ref> Additionally, he proposed a simple mitigation strategy for a systematic gate error in IBMQ quantum computers<ref>{{Cite arXiv|title=Simple Mitigation Strategy for a Systematic Gate Error in IBMQ|first1=Daniel|last1=Bultrini|first2=Max Hunter|last2=Gordon|first3=Esperanza|last3=López|first4=Germȧn|last4=Sierra|date=December 10, 2020|class=quant-ph |eprint=2012.00831}}</ref> and demonstrated the implementation of data-driven error mitigation techniques to simulate quench dynamics on a digital quantum computer.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/2058-9565/ac0e7a/meta|doi=10.1088/2058-9565/ac0e7a |title=Simulating quench dynamics on a digital quantum computer with data-driven error mitigation |date=2021 |last1=Sopena |first1=Alejandro |last2=Gordon |first2=Max Hunter |last3=Sierra |first3=Germán |last4=López |first4=Esperanza |journal=Quantum Science and Technology |volume=6 |issue=4 |page=045003 |arxiv=2103.12680 |bibcode=2021QS&T....6d5003S |s2cid=232320788 }}</ref>

===Quantum games===
In 2022, Sierra, together with A. Bera and S. Singha Roy, demonstrated a connection between the ground state of a topological Hamiltonian and the optimal strategy in a causal order game, where the maximum violation of the classical bound is associated with a second-order [[quantum phase transition]].<ref name=mmm/> Furthermore, working in conjunction with D. Centeno led to the development of several quantum versions of the Morra game, known as Chinos in Spain.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/2399-6528/ac7434/meta|doi=10.1088/2399-6528/ac7434 |title=General quantum Chinos games |date=2022 |last1=Centeno |first1=Daniel |last2=Sierra |first2=Germán |journal=Journal of Physics Communications |volume=6 |issue=7 |page=075009 |arxiv=2112.05175 |bibcode=2022JPhCo...6g5009C |s2cid=250739663 }}</ref>
